newsitem.title: UK: Dixons jumps five pct on top-end profits.
newsitem.headline: Dixons jumps five pct on top-end profits.

text.p: Shares in Dixons Group Plc jumped five percent in pre-market trading on Wednesday, boosted by annual profits that came in at the upper end of expectations and on an upbeat trading statement, dealers said.
At 0714 GMT, Dixons traded 25-1/2p higher at 518p, against the backdrop of a slightly higher gain indicated for the FTSE 100.
"It's up on the figures," on profits and current sales, one dealer said.
Dixons, Britain's leading electricals retailer, said profits before tax and exceptional items for the 53 weeks to May 3, 1997 rose to 190.2 million stg, from 135.2 million stg.
Analysts expected profits between 180 and 196.5 million stg.

In the past nine weeks, retail division sales gained 32 percent overall and by 17 percent on a like-for-like basis, the company said. It expected to create around 3,000 new jobs over the year, about the same as in the previous 12 months.
The retailer pointed to windfall gains from building society flotations for boosting recent sales.
